original_question: Does there exist a group G that contains a family(Gn)n∈N of finite-index subgroups such that for every n there is a homomorphism fn: Gn → Z whose kernel is of type Fn, but not of type Fn+1?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.119 in the section “New Problems (21st issue, 2026)”
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s exact formulation. It correctly asks for: an ambient group G; a family (G_n) indexed by n∈N; each G_n being finite-index in G; for each n, a homomorphism f_n:G_n→Z; and the exact finiteness-property gap that ker(f_n) is of type F_n but not of type F_{n+1}. This matches Problem 21.119 almost verbatim.
missing_details: The question is not fully stand-alone because it does not define what “type F_n” means. In the paper, this terminology is defined elsewhere: a group is of type F_n if it has a classifying space with finite n-skeleton, with F_1 meaning finitely generated and F_2 meaning finitely presented.
It should explicitly say that n ranges over the positive integers (n≥1).
It is helpful to state explicitly that each G_n is a subgroup of G of finite index.
For complete stand-alone clarity, “homomorphism” should be read as “group homomorphism”.

No extra hypothesis on the ambient group G is stated in Problem 21.119 itself; in particular, one should not add assumptions such as G being of type F_∞ unless one intentionally departs from the paper’s exact formulation.
refined_question: Does there exist a group G containing a sequence of finite-index subgroups (G_n)_{n\ge 1} such that, for each positive integer n, there exists a group homomorphism f_n:G_n\to \mathbb{Z} whose kernel is of type F_n but not of type F_{n+1}? Here, a group is of type F_n if it admits a classifying space K(-,1) with finite n-skeleton.
justification: Within arXiv:1401.0300, the exact statement your draft is targeting is Problem 21.119, which asks precisely for a group G with finite-index subgroups G_n and homomorphisms f_n:G_n→Z whose kernels are of type F_n but not F_{n+1}. Your draft is therefore already very faithful to the paper. The only substantive omission, if the question is to stand on its own, is the definition of the finiteness property F_n. That definition is supplied elsewhere in the same paper, in Problem 21.146. Since Problem 21.119 itself is stated without additional hypotheses on G, adding conditions such as “G is of type F_∞” would move away from the exact formulation appearing in this paper.
